raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

`MHCPreOp` and `MHCFusedPostPreOp` accept `norm_weight` / `norm_eps` and their callers expect a normalized `layer_input`. On `main` the unfused paths disagree about who applies that norm:

| path | applies the norm? |
|---|---|
| `forward_cuda` | yes, inside the fused kernel |
| `forward_hip` with AITER or TileLang | yes, inside the fused kernel |
| `forward_hip` fallback | yes, `_apply_mhc_norm` on top of `forward_native`'s output |
| `forward_native` | **no** — takes both parameters and ignores them |

`CustomOp.forward_oot` falls back to `forward_native`, so every out-of-tree backend loses the normalization. The failure is silent: nothing raises, no NaN appears, the numbers are just wrong.

I hit this running GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2. All 45 mHC layers lost their input norm; generation degraded to unrelated tokens with a near-uniform logit distribution (top-1 probability 0.99%, top-10 nearly equiprobable), while every per-layer NaN/Inf check stayed clean. @shiweijiezero hit the same thing independently on the MetaX backend.

## Change

`forward_native` of both ops now applies `_apply_mhc_norm` to the mix it returns. The HIP fallback branches, which used to apply it on top of `forward_native`, now return `forward_native`'s result directly — otherwise they would normalize twice. That is the shape `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` already has. The AITER and TileLang branches are unchanged. (HIP fallback fix suggested by @shiweijiezero.)

Not in scope: `forward_cpu` does not go through `forward_native`; it calls `mhc_pre_cpu`, which also accepts `norm_weight` / `norm_eps` without applying them. Its only in-tree caller today, the DeepSeek-V4 CPU model, passes no norm weight, and I cannot build the CPU kernel to test a change there.

## Test Plan

Two tests in `tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py`, each parametrized over both unfused paths — `forward_native`, and `forward_hip` with AITER and TileLang disabled — for 8 cases in total:

- `test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once`
- `test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once`

Each compares `layer_input` against the `norm_weight=None` mix normalized once by hand, and asserts the two differ *before* comparing, so the test cannot pass vacuously. On the HIP fallback they also check that with `norm_weight=None` every output matches `forward_native` exactly (suggested by @shiweijiezero). Every other mHC test is gated on `HAS_TILELANG_MHC` or AITER, which is why neither unfused path had coverage.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k unfused_applies_norm_once
```

## Test Result

The same 8 tests against three versions of `mhc.py`:

```
main (forward_native skips the norm)
FAILED test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-1-native]
FAILED test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-8-native]
FAILED test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-1-native]
FAILED test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-8-native]
4 failed, 4 passed

first revision of this PR (native norm added, HIP fallback still re-normalizing)
FAILED test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-1-hip_fallback]
FAILED test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-8-hip_fallback]
FAILED test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-1-hip_fallback]
FAILED test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once[4-4096-8-hip_fallback]
4 failed, 4 passed

this PR
8 passed
```

The whole file on this branch, rebased onto `main` @ `2798f668`: `192 passed, 136 skipped` (the skips need TileLang or AITER).

The magnitude of the difference, measured on CPU with GLM-5.3-Flash's shapes (hidden 4096, hc_mult 4, 20 sinkhorn iterations):

```
raw mix    (what forward_native returns) std=0.020015
normalized (what callers expect)         std=1.006403
max abs diff = 3.897   ->  50x in standard deviation
```

End-to-end on Gaudi 2 with GLM-5.3-Flash, greedy decoding, prompt `中国的首都是` ("The capital of China is"):

| | output |
|---|---|
| before | `(e цErrorIdError(e ?以前?aid?Souomeaisaubaub` |
| after | `北京，北京是中国的政治、文化中心，也是中国的` |

Single-token top-1 probability went from 0.99% (`'Å'`) to 43.1% (`'北京'`). That run used the first revision, whose `forward_native` is unchanged since; the review change touches only the HIP fallback, which Gaudi never executes.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both changed files.

---

*AI disclosure: this change was developed with assistance from Claude (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line, reproduced the bug and validated the fix end-to-end on real hardware, and ran the tests myself.*

Hi guys, thanks for working on this. We independently encountered the same missing normalization while running GLM-5.3-Flash on the MetaX backend.

There is a related issue in the HIP fallback branches of both `MHCPreOp` and `MHCFusedPostPreOp`: they pass `norm_weight` and `norm_eps` to `forward_native`, then apply `_apply_mhc_norm` to its output again. With the native fix in this PR, those fallback branches normalize twice.

Could both HIP fallback branches return `self.forward_native(...)` directly, keeping the existing arguments? The AITER and TileLang branches can remain unchanged.

The additional changes in `vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py` would look like this, with unchanged arguments abbreviated:

```diff
# MHCPreOp.forward_hip
-            post_mix, comb_mix, layer_input = self.forward_native(
+            return self.forward_native(
                 ...
                 norm_weight,
                 norm_eps,
             )
-            return (
-                post_mix,
-                comb_mix,
-                _apply_mhc_norm(layer_input, norm_weight, norm_eps),
-            )

# MHCFusedPostPreOp.forward_hip
-        residual_cur, post_mix_cur, comb_mix_cur, layer_input_cur = self.forward_native(
+        return self.forward_native(
             ...
             norm_weight,
             norm_eps,
         )
-        return (
-            residual_cur,
-            post_mix_cur,
-            comb_mix_cur,
-            _apply_mhc_norm(layer_input_cur, norm_weight, norm_eps),
-        )
```

This preserves the original HIP fallback computation: normalization still happens exactly once, now inside the native implementation.

We checked the behavior using the full vLLM modules and the real `vllm.ir.ops.rms_norm`. A local extension of `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py` covered eight cases: both operators, native/HIP fallback, and with/without `norm_weight`.

With the patch at `acf84cab`, the two HIP fallback cases with normalization weights fail. Returning the native results directly makes all eight cases pass. These checks ran on CPU with optimized-kernel availability flags disabled; GPU-only model imports in the test file were deferred to their consuming tests for CPU collection.

The existing HIP fallback tests would also be useful regression coverage alongside the new native tests. Would you be open to including this adjustment here? We’re happy to share the full diff and regression cases, or open a small PR against your branch if that would be helpful.

Confirmed on my side: with `forward_native` normalizing, both HIP fallback
branches applied `_apply_mhc_norm` a second time. I took your change as written:
both fallbacks now return `self.forward_native(...)` with the existing
arguments, and the AITER and TileLang branches are untouched. That is also the
shape `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` already has. You are credited as co-author
on the commit (`ff119eb2`), and the branch is rebased onto current `main`.

this PR before your fix (acf84cab)   4 failed (hip_fallback),  4 passed

Two differences from your eight cases, so you can tell whether yours are still
worth adding: mine vary the token count rather than the presence of

         norm_eps=norm_eps,
     )

files.patch:
@@ -33,6 +33,7 @@
     MHCFusedPostPreOp,
     MHCPreDelayedOp,
     MHCPreOp,
+    _apply_mhc_norm,
 )
 from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.model import (
     DeepseekV4DecoderLayer,
@@ -1755,3 +1756,121 @@ def test_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_falls_back_for_large_batches():
 
     assert not rocm_aiter_ops.mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_prefers_unfused(1)
     assert rocm_aiter_ops.mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_prefers_unfused(1 << 20)
+
+
+def _mhc_pre_inputs(
+    num_tokens: int, hidden_size: int, hc_mult: int, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+):
+    """Inputs shaped the way mhc_pre_torch's own assertions require."""
+    hc_mult3 = hc_mult * 2 + hc_mult * hc_mult
+    hc_hidden = hc_mult * hidden_size
+    residual = (torch.randn(num_tokens, hc_mult, hidden_size) * 0.02).to(dtype)
+    fn = (torch.randn(hc_mult3, hc_hidden) * 0.02).to(torch.float32)
+    hc_scale = (torch.randn(3) * 0.1).to(torch.float32)
+    hc_base = (torch.randn(hc_mult3) * 0.1).to(torch.float32)
+    return residual, fn, hc_scale, hc_base
+
+
+def _forward(op, path, monkeypatch, *args, **kwargs):
+    """forward_native, or forward_hip on ROCm without AITER or TileLang."""
+    if path == "native":
+        return op.forward_native(*args, **kwargs)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mhc_layers, "HAS_TILELANG_MHC", False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mhc_layers, "HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED", False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mhc_layers, "_aiter_mhc_supported", lambda *a, **k: False)
+    return op.forward_hip(*args, **kwargs)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", ["native", "hip_fallback"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("hidden_size", [4096])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("hc_mult", [4])
+def test_mhc_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once(
+    path, num_tokens, hidden_size, hc_mult, default_vllm_config, monkeypatch
+):
+    """The unfused paths must return layer_input normalized exactly once.
+
+    forward_oot falls back to forward_native, and so does forward_hip without
+    AITER or TileLang. Missing the norm is silent -- no NaN, no exception, just
+    an un-normalized residual mix fed into attention and MLP/MoE -- and applying
+    it twice is just as silent.
+    """
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    residual, fn, hc_scale, hc_base = _mhc_pre_inputs(num_tokens, hidden_size, hc_mult)
+    norm_weight = (torch.randn(hidden_size) * 0.1 + 1.0).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    norm_eps = 1e-6
+
+    op = MHCPreOp()
+    args = (residual, fn, hc_scale, hc_base)
+    kwargs = dict(
+        rms_eps=1e-6,
+        hc_pre_eps=1e-6,
+        hc_sinkhorn_eps=1e-6,
+        hc_post_mult_value=1.0,
+        sinkhorn_repeat=20,
+        n_splits=1,
+        norm_eps=norm_eps,
+    )
+    # Without a norm weight the raw mix comes back untouched.
+    raw_outputs = op.forward_native(*args, norm_weight=None, **kwargs)
+    raw_mix = raw_outputs[-1]
+    if path == "hip_fallback":
+        actual = _forward(op, path, monkeypatch, *args, norm_weight=None, **kwargs)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, raw_outputs)
+
+    _, _, layer_input = _forward(
+        op, path, monkeypatch, *args, norm_weight=norm_weight, **kwargs
+    )
+    expected = _apply_mhc_norm(raw_mix, norm_weight, norm_eps)
+
+    # Guard against a vacuous assertion: the norm must actually change the mix.
+    assert not torch.allclose(raw_mix.float(), expected.float(), atol=1e-4)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        layer_input.float(), expected.float(), atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", ["native", "hip_fallback"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("hidden_size", [4096])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("hc_mult", [4])
+def test_mhc_fused_post_pre_unfused_applies_norm_once(
+    path, num_tokens, hidden_size, hc_mult, default_vllm_config, monkeypatch
+):
+    """Same contract for the fused post+pre op."""
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    residual, fn, hc_scale, hc_base = _mhc_pre_inputs(num_tokens, hidden_size, hc_mult)
+    x = (torch.randn(num_tokens, hidden_size) * 0.02).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    # post_layer_mix broadcasts against x.unsqueeze(-2) -> [T, 1, hidden]
+    post_layer_mix = (torch.randn(num_tokens, hc_mult, 1) * 0.1).to(torch.float32)
+    comb_res_mix = (torch.randn(num_tokens, hc_mult, hc_mult) * 0.1).to(torch.float32)
+    norm_weight = (torch.randn(hidden_size) * 0.1 + 1.0).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    norm_eps = 1e-6
+
+    op = MHCFusedPostPreOp()
+    args = (x, residual, post_layer_mix, comb_res_mix, fn, hc_scale, hc_base)
+    kwargs = dict(
+        rms_eps=1e-6,
+        hc_pre_eps=1e-6,
+        hc_sinkhorn_eps=1e-6,
+        hc_post_mult_value=1.0,
+        sinkhorn_repeat=20,
+        n_splits=1,
+        tile_n=1,
+        norm_eps=norm_eps,
+    )
+    raw_outputs = op.forward_native(*args, norm_weight=None, **kwargs)
+    raw_mix = raw_outputs[-1]
+    if path == "hip_fallback":
+        actual = _forward(op, path, monkeypatch, *args, norm_weight=None, **kwargs)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, raw_outputs)
+
+    *_, layer_input = _forward(
+        op, path, monkeypatch, *args, norm_weight=norm_weight, **kwargs
+    )
+    expected = _apply_mhc_norm(raw_mix, norm_weight, norm_eps)
+
+    assert not torch.allclose(raw_mix.float(), expected.float(), atol=1e-4)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        layer_input.float(), expected.float(), atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2
+    )

@@ -199,7 +199,7 @@ def forward_hip(
                 norm_eps,
             )
         else:
-            post_mix, comb_mix, layer_input = self.forward_native(
+            return self.forward_native(
                 residual,
                 fn,
                 hc_scale,
@@ -213,11 +213,6 @@ def forward_hip(
                 norm_weight,
                 norm_eps,
             )
-            return (
-                post_mix,
-                comb_mix,
-                _apply_mhc_norm(layer_input, norm_weight, norm_eps),
-            )
 
     def forward_native(
         self,
@@ -234,7 +229,7 @@ def forward_native(
         norm_weight: torch.Tensor | None = None,
         norm_eps: float = 0.0,

Hi guys, thanks for working on this. We independently encountered the same missing normalization while running GLM-5.3-Flash on the MetaX backend.

There is a related issue in the HIP fallback branches of both `MHCPreOp` and `MHCFusedPostPreOp`: they pass `norm_weight` and `norm_eps` to `forward_native`, then apply `_apply_mhc_norm` to its output again. With the native fix in this PR, those fallback branches normalize twice.

Could both HIP fallback branches return `self.forward_native(...)` directly, keeping the existing arguments? The AITER and TileLang branches can remain unchanged.

The additional changes in `vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py` would look like this, with unchanged arguments abbreviated:

```diff
# MHCPreOp.forward_hip
-            post_mix, comb_mix, layer_input = self.forward_native(
+            return self.forward_native(
                 ...
                 norm_weight,
                 norm_eps,
             )
-            return (
-                post_mix,
-                comb_mix,
-                _apply_mhc_norm(layer_input, norm_weight, norm_eps),
-            )

# MHCFusedPostPreOp.forward_hip
-        residual_cur, post_mix_cur, comb_mix_cur, layer_input_cur = self.forward_native(
+        return self.forward_native(
             ...
             norm_weight,
             norm_eps,
         )
-        return (
-            residual_cur,
-            post_mix_cur,
-            comb_mix_cur,
-            _apply_mhc_norm(layer_input_cur, norm_weight, norm_eps),
-        )
```

This preserves the original HIP fallback computation: normalization still happens exactly once, now inside the native implementation.

We checked the behavior using the full vLLM modules and the real `vllm.ir.ops.rms_norm`. A local extension of `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py` covered eight cases: both operators, native/HIP fallback, and with/without `norm_weight`.

With the patch at `acf84cab`, the two HIP fallback cases with normalization weights fail. Returning the native results directly makes all eight cases pass. These checks ran on CPU with optimized-kernel availability flags disabled; GPU-only model imports in the test file were deferred to their consuming tests for CPU collection.

The existing HIP fallback tests would also be useful regression coverage alongside the new native tests. Would you be open to including this adjustment here? We’re happy to share the full diff and regression cases, or open a small PR against your branch if that would be helpful.

@shiweijiezero You are right, thank you — and good to hear it is not just Gaudi.

Confirmed on my side: with `forward_native` normalizing, both HIP fallback
branches applied `_apply_mhc_norm` a second time. I took your change as written:
both fallbacks now return `self.forward_native(...)` with the existing
arguments, and the AITER and TileLang branches are untouched. That is also the
shape `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` already has. You are credited as co-author
on the commit (`ff119eb2`), and the branch is rebased onto current `main`.

For the tests I parametrized the two existing ones over both unfused paths —
`forward_native`, and `forward_hip` with `HAS_TILELANG_MHC`,
`HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED` and `_aiter_mhc_supported` patched off — so 8 cases across
both ops. Against three versions of `mhc.py`:

```
main                                 4 failed (native),        4 passed
this PR before your fix (acf84cab)   4 failed (hip_fallback),  4 passed
this PR now                          8 passed
```

which matches what you saw at `acf84cab`. The whole `test_mhc_kernels.py` gives
`192 passed, 121 skipped` on this branch.

Two differences from your eight cases, so you can tell whether yours are still
worth adding: mine vary the token count rather than the presence of
`norm_weight`, so there is no separate `norm_weight=None` case per path (each
test does call `forward_native` without it to build the expected value, but that
pins the native path only). And I ran them on a CUDA machine, so I left the
module-level GPU-only imports alone. If you want the `norm_weight=None` fallback
cases in, I am happy to take them here.

I also corrected the description while I was at it. It claimed vLLM's CPU
backend was affected too; it is not — `forward_cpu` has its own path through
`mhc_pre_cpu` and never reaches `forward_native`. The affected backends are the
out-of-tree ones that fall back to `forward_native`, like yours and Gaudi.
